angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 3,145,944 km at 122.41 pc = 0.34 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.1691 +/- 0.0181 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 122.41 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 4.522 (4.431 to 4.613) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 3,145,944 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.550 (1.509 to 1.590) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4944 +/- 1.3 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 845335158256083584: teff_gspphot 4944.016 K (16th-84th percentiles 4942.746-4945.3706), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 845335158256083584: teff_gspphot 4944.016 K (16th-84th percentiles 4942.746-4945.3706), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/aniara.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.318, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 102956 (pscomppars): spectral type G5, from Cannon & Pickering 1918 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1918AnHar..91....1C/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 102956: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 102956 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.19 dex, from Johnson et al. 2010 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010ApJ...721L.153J/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 102956 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 1.06446, from Johnson et al. 2010 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010ApJ...721L.153J/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 102956 (pscomppars): age 2.3 Gyr, from Johnson et al. 2010 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010ApJ...721L.153J/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, HD 102956: projected rotation speed 1.6 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2018ApJ...860..109G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
